title: MANIFST: metadata schema and process design for a catalogue of 236 analytical techniques

conventions.language: Australian English. Sentence case for headings, field labels and value names. No em dashes, en dashes or double hyphens.
conventions.value_ids: Value ids are lower case strings, written with spaces and without the characters ; : = | & and the sequence ::, because those are used in cell syntax. The display name is the id with its first letter capitalised. Evidence status keeps the capitalised values used in the earlier reports.
conventions.any_and_unknown: any means the facet does not matter for the technique. It is written only in a technique's cell and is never a value of the material. unknown is a real state of the material and is listed as a value only where it can occur. A material with unknown on a facet cannot meet a requires on that facet; the skill asks the user or reports the requirement as unmet.
conventions.single_valued_fields: A field with values_mutually_exclusive true has categories that do not overlap, so a material takes exactly one value (material_cardinality exactly one). Where values_mutually_exclusive is false, the material may take several values at once and the tagger lists each one the technique needs.
conventions.technique_cell_type: For input profile facets the technique's cell type is multiple values even when the material takes one value, because a technique can accept several alternatives.
conventions.terms: One term per concept: technique, topic, family, phase.
conventions.status: Draft. Gate classes, tag values and the process design are inference unless a basis says sourced. Tested on five hand-written jobs and four intake inputs; not tested on real jobs end to end.
conventions.family_names: Family names are sentence case labels (for example Frame the question) and are not value ids, so the lower case rule for value ids does not apply to them.

gate_classes.definition: The technique is removed when the material or job does not meet its requires value, or when the material is unknown on that facet and the user cannot supply it.
gate_classes.label: Always applies

gate_classes.definition: The requirement applies only under the condition stated in the field definition; otherwise the field is ignored.
gate_classes.label: Applies in some cases

gate_classes.definition: Never removes a technique. It changes ranking only.
gate_classes.label: Changes the order

gate_classes.definition: Never removes a technique. It raises a warning shown with the shortlist.
gate_classes.label: Raises a warning

gate_classes.definition: The field is not used for matching.
gate_classes.label: Not used

cell_syntax.facet cell: A cell is either the single word any, or items separated by ; where each item is requires=<value> or prefers=<value>. Several requires items in one cell are alternatives (the material needs at least one). A prefers item never excludes; it raises the technique in ranking when matched. Values come from the field's value list. For an ordered field, requires=X means X or any value after it in the list.
cell_syntax.plain: Plain value or values, separated by ; where the field allows several.
cell_syntax.artefact: Items separated by ;, each written as <artefact type>:<state>, with type and state from the artefact_types list.
cell_syntax.relation: Items separated by ;. Each item is written as relation :: target :: reason for related_techniques, where target is a technique ID or family:<family name>. In requires, items are technique IDs or artefact:<type>:<state>. none if empty.
cell_syntax.rule: Exclusions separated by ;. Each exclusion is clauses joined by &; a clause is <key>=<value> or <key>=<value1>|<value2>. The technique is removed when every clause of any one exclusion is true for the job. An optional :: reason follows the last clause. none if empty.
cell_syntax.tier_check: Items separated by ;, each written as <tier>:<check code>, with tier from the tiers list and the code from the check library.

fields.label: Technique ID
fields.definition: Stable identifier of one technique: the family prefix and a running number, as used in the two earlier reports.

basis.note: Identifier format follows the two earlier reports. It is a catalogue convention, not a standard.

fields.tagging_rule: Copy the identifier from the earlier report. Never renumber or reuse an identifier.

fields.label: Technique name
fields.definition: Preferred name of the technique, followed by alternative names in brackets, separated by semicolons.

basis.note: Distinctive names and the words users use help selection (Anthropic tool search guidance); the effect on technique catalogues is untested.

fields.tagging_rule: Use the name in the earlier report. Put alternative names and common abbreviations in brackets so that a search on the user's own words can match.

fields.label: Family
fields.definition: The family the technique belongs to. A technique has exactly one family, which groups techniques by the operation they perform and does not order them.

values.definition: Acts on the question and its terms before evidence is examined.
Splits a topic into parts, sorts items, places them in a structure or models relationships.
Sets one case, period, standard or forecaster against another.
Traces causal chains, estimates effects or tests whether a claim is true.
Grades sources, combines evidence and analyses documents, text or data.
Projects a quantity, generates alternative futures or monitors for change.
Assesses who matters, which option is best and what could go wrong.
Tests the current view or plan by arguing against it.
Turns raw text, tables or reports into a form that can be analysed.
Measures, summarises or models prepared data or text.
Combines or reconciles results from two or more sources.
Checks the accuracy, reliability or validity of extracted or modelled results.

basis.note: The eight earlier families are the note authors' reconciliation of ten groupings, and the four later families are an extension. No source supplies this taxonomy.

fields.tagging_rule: Use the family given in the earlier report. Do not infer a new family.

fields.label: Purpose
fields.definition: One plain sentence stating what the technique does and what artefact it produces.

basis.note: A clear statement of purpose and of when to use it is the best-supported description element (Hasan et al., abstract only).

fields.tagging_rule: Write one sentence in plain words that starts with a verb. Name the artefact produced.

fields.label: Use when
fields.definition: A short phrase, in the words a user would use, describing the situations in which the technique is the right choice.

basis.note: The skills documentation requires a statement of when to use a skill; per-technique use of this text is untested.

fields.tagging_rule: Write one phrase starting with a user situation, for example a question a user might ask. Do not repeat the purpose.

fields.label: Representation
fields.definition: How the material is stored: whether it has a fixed schema, a loose structure or none. This is a different property from content type and from document genre.

values.definition: Fixed fields or columns with a declared schema, such as a database table or CSV file.
Self-describing records with variable fields, such as JSON, XML, or documents with headings and tables.
No schema; free text or media in which structure must be extracted.

basis.note: The DCMI Dataset type is the nearest standard definition of structured. No standard defines the three-way split, so every value here is inference.

fields.tagging_rule: List the representations the technique needs as requires, and any it handles better as prefers. Write any when the technique runs on whatever form the material is in.

fields.label: Content type
fields.definition: The kind of content in the material. Values are not mutually exclusive, because one item can have several (a geospatial time series is geospatial and a time series); tag every value the technique needs.

values.definition: Natural language words.
Rows and columns of values.
Values indexed by time order.
Values tied to coordinates or areas.
Nodes and the links between them.
Still images.
Sound recordings.
Moving images with or without sound.

basis.note: Carrier values (text, image, audio, video) and data form values (tabular, time series, geospatial, network) mix in the standards. They are kept in one field and tagged as a set.

fields.tagging_rule: List each content type the technique operates on as requires. Write any only if the technique works on every content type.

fields.label: Unit of analysis
fields.definition: The unit that one output of the technique describes and that the material must supply or allow to be extracted. Each value names a different unit; one material can offer several.

values.definition: One row, case or respondent.
One measured attribute across records.
One report, article, page or file.
One assertion that can be true or false.
One origin of information, such as a publisher, dataset or person.
A whole table or collection treated as one object.
A subject or question, not tied to one item.

basis.note: DDI has an analysis unit element, but its vocabulary was not opened. The value list is carried over from the earlier reports with variable added.

fields.tagging_rule: List the unit the technique works on as requires. A claim-level technique requires claim unless the material is already split into claims.

fields.label: Variable types
fields.definition: The measurement types present among the variables. Advisory and applied per variable, not as a dataset-level gate, because scale type depends on the question and the extra information available.

values.definition: Unordered categories, including binary.
Ordered categories with unequal or unknown spacing.
Equal spacing with an arbitrary zero.
Equal spacing with a true zero.
Non-negative integer counts, or fractions bounded by 0 and 1 such as percentages.

basis.note: Stevens' four types plus counts and counted fractions from Mosteller and Tukey. Velleman and Wilkinson dispute using scale type as a hard gate, so this field only raises a warning.

fields.tagging_rule: List the types the technique's estimator assumes as prefers. Write any if the technique does not depend on measurement type. Binary variables are tagged nominal.

fields.label: Time structure
fields.definition: How observations relate to time. The DDI Time Method terms are the base, flattened so that no value contains another; continuous stream is not a DDI term.

values.definition: One observation of each unit at one point in time.
Different samples of the same population at several points in time.
The same sample of units observed at several points in time.
A group defined by a shared event or birth period, followed over time.
Externally observable aggregate indicators recorded in time order, such as economic indicators or vital statistics.
Observations arriving without a fixed period (not a DDI term).
No time dimension is relevant to the material.
The time structure cannot be determined.

basis.note: DDI Time Method 1.2 terms. Continuous stream is added as inference because DDI has no value for it. The gate is conditional: it applies only when the question concerns change over time.

fields.tagging_rule: Require panel or cohort if the technique follows the same units over time. Write any if the technique does not use time.

fields.label: Collection basis
fields.definition: How the units in the material were selected. It decides whether estimates for a population are valid; descriptive use is unaffected.

values.definition: Units selected with known, non-zero chances by a random mechanism.
Units selected non-randomly to fill preset group counts.
Units chosen by the researcher for stated characteristics.
Units chosen because they were easy for the researcher to reach.
Units recruited through referrals from earlier units, such as snowball sampling.
Units that chose to take part, including opt-in panels and volunteer responses.
A design that combines both kinds.
Every unit in the universe is included.
Not collected as a sample: administrative, transactional, sensor or scraped data.
The selection process is not documented.

sources.name: AAPOR Non-probability Sampling Task Force report 2013

basis.note: DDI Sampling Procedure and AAPOR terms. Non-sampled is added as inference: DDI has no value for administrative, transactional, sensor or scraped data beyond Other. Availability or convenience, and self-selected or opt-in, overlap in AAPOR usage, so the definitions here separate them by who initiates selection.

fields.tagging_rule: Require probability or census if the technique produces population estimates with confidence intervals. Write any for descriptive techniques.

fields.label: Access depth
fields.definition: The deepest level of detail the material gives access to. Values are ordered from narrative only to record-level, and a requirement means that level or deeper.

values.definition: Prose description with no tables of figures.
Published totals, rates or summary tables.
Underlying rows or records.

basis.note: No standard facet exists. Cochrane shows that depth differs by document type; DCAT records who may access, not depth.

fields.tagging_rule: Require the shallowest level the technique can work from. Record-level techniques such as regression or deduplication require record-level.

fields.label: Number of sources
fields.definition: Whether the technique works within one source or needs several. Separate from linkage.

values.definition: A single source.
Two or more separate sources.

basis.note: No standard value set exists. Carried over from the earlier reports, where it was called sources needed.

fields.tagging_rule: Write requires=two or more for cross-source techniques. Write any if the technique works with one source or many.

fields.label: Linkage
fields.definition: Whether units in different sources can be joined through a shared identifier. Separate from the number of sources.

values.definition: A key such as an ID, code or name exists in both sources.
No usable key; matching would need inexact matching.
Only one source.
Not yet checked.

basis.note: No standard value set exists; dcat:inSeries and dcterms:source are the nearest terms.

fields.tagging_rule: Require shared identifier available for joins and record linkage. Write any if the technique does not join sources.

fields.label: Volume class
fields.definition: Whether a person can read the whole material or it needs automation. It is separate from unit of analysis.

values.definition: Small enough for a person to read in full in the time available.
Too large to read in full; processing needs code or a model.

basis.note: DCAT byteSize is the standard volume term; this two-value class is derived from it and from format.

fields.tagging_rule: Require needs automation for techniques that only work at scale, or readable by a person for techniques done by hand. Write any otherwise.

fields.label: Data condition flags
fields.definition: Known quality problems in the material, from the ABS Data Quality Framework dimensions. None known and unknown cannot be combined with other values. A technique that repairs a problem requires its flag.

values.definition: No problem has been identified.
Condition has not been assessed.
Values or records are absent.
The material contradicts itself or other sources.
Variable meaning, units or collection process are not documented.
The reference period is too old for the question.
Units appear more than once.
Values are known or suspected to be inaccurate or imprecise.

basis.note: Nearest ABS dimensions: timeliness (out of date), coherence (inconsistent), interpretability (undocumented), accuracy (measurement error). ABS definitions beyond timeliness were not obtained. Duplicated and measurement error are added from the ISO 25012 gap analysis.

fields.tagging_rule: Require a flag if the technique exists to handle it, for example imputation requires missing data. Use not_for_rules to exclude a technique that fails when a flag is present. Write any if condition does not matter.

fields.label: Producer interest
fields.definition: The relationship of the producer of a source to its funder or subject. It changes how much weight a result deserves, not whether a technique runs.

values.definition: The producer has no stake in the finding.
Funded by a party with an interest in the finding.
The producer sells a product or service the finding supports.
Not determined.

sources.name: Adams, Smart and Huff 2017 via CORE

basis.note: No standard value set exists. AACODS objectivity and Cochrane vested interests are the nearest published criteria.

fields.tagging_rule: Write any for nearly all techniques. Require a value only if the technique appraises it, in which case set appraises_source_credibility to yes.

fields.label: Source dependence
fields.definition: Whether sources rest on the same upstream origin. It changes the weight of agreement between sources.

values.definition: Sources were produced separately from different evidence.
One source copies, cites or is built from another.
Not determined.

sources.name: Treur et al. 2024, guide for planning triangulation studies

basis.note: No standard term exists. Kuorikoski and Marchionni treat independence as relative to the claim.

fields.tagging_rule: Write any for nearly all techniques. Require independent only for corroboration techniques that count agreement between sources.

fields.label: Origin
fields.definition: How close the source is to the original event or data. It changes the weight of a result.

values.definition: Original account, data or research.
Interprets or reports primary material.
Collects and distils primary and secondary sources, such as an encyclopedia or handbook.
Not determined.

basis.note: Primary, secondary and tertiary follow the library definitions; no archival definition was verified. Unknown is added as inference.

fields.tagging_rule: Write any unless the technique appraises provenance. Record derived-from links in the data source inventory, not here.

fields.label: Document genre
fields.definition: The form of a document, chosen by the document's form and not by its publisher. Where two values fit, use the earlier one in the list.

values.definition: Systematic review, meta-analysis or overview of reviews.
Report of original research, peer reviewed or preprint.
Legislation, regulation or court decision.
Report or statistical release by a public body.
Report by a company, think tank, industry body or non-government organisation.
Encyclopedia, textbook or handbook.
Journalism, opinion or blog post.
Interview, hearing or meeting record.
Short public posts and replies.
A dataset or table with at most brief documentation.
Fits none of the above.

sources.name: Adams, Smart and Huff 2017 via CORE

basis.note: Informed by DataCite resource types and grey literature tiers. The list and the precedence rule are the schema designer's inference.

fields.tagging_rule: Write any for nearly all techniques. List genres only for appraisal techniques that apply to one genre, for example a systematic review appraisal tool.

fields.label: Appraises source credibility
fields.definition: Whether the technique appraises source credibility, independence or sponsorship. When yes, producer interest, source dependence and origin become required inputs for this technique.

values.definition: The technique appraises credibility, independence or sponsorship.
The technique does not.

basis.note: Follows the research finding that the weight facets gate only techniques that test credibility.

fields.tagging_rule: Write yes if the technique's purpose is to grade, test or compare the credibility, independence or sponsorship of sources. Otherwise write no.

fields.label: Language
fields.definition: Whether the material is in one language or several. Language-specific tools are recorded in requires_minimum.

values.definition: All material is in one language.
The material has more than one language.

basis.note: DCAT recommends ISO 639 language codes. The two-value class is inference; text-analysis preconditions such as language support were not researched.

fields.tagging_rule: Require multiple only for cross-language techniques such as translation checks. Write any for all others.

fields.label: Privacy
fields.definition: Whether the material contains personal information, applied as a pre-filter before matching. On a technique, the cell lists the classes the technique may run on; any means all.

values.definition: Nothing that could identify an individual.
Information or an opinion that could identify an individual.
Personal information about racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religion, union membership, sexual orientation, criminal record, health or genetic data, or some biometric data.
Not assessed.

sources.name: OAIC, Australian Privacy Principles quick reference

basis.note: Categories follow OAIC definitions under the Australian Privacy Principles. Unknown is added as inference and is treated as the most restrictive class.

fields.tagging_rule: Write any unless the technique links, discloses or re-identifies individuals, in which case list only the classes it may run on, using requires.

fields.label: Security classification
fields.definition: The protective marking of the material, applied as a pre-filter before matching. On a technique, the cell lists the markings it may be used with. Not used in matching or asked at intake: all 236 techniques are tagged any. Kept so that a deployment can add a requirement later.

values.definition: No protective marking.
Marked OFFICIAL under the PSPF.
Marked OFFICIAL: Sensitive under the PSPF.
Any marking above OFFICIAL: Sensitive; the full list is unconfirmed.
Not assessed.

sources.name: PSPF Policy 8, sensitive and classified information

basis.note: OFFICIAL and OFFICIAL: Sensitive are confirmed. The two PSPF pages disagree on the number of classifications, so the higher value is not subdivided. Unclassified and unknown are added as inference.

fields.tagging_rule: Write any unless the technique requires copying material to an uncontrolled service, in which case list only the lowest markings using requires.

fields.label: Licence
fields.definition: The terms under which the material may be used, applied as a pre-filter before matching. It is a different instrument from privacy and security. Not used in matching or asked at intake: all 236 techniques are tagged any. Kept so that a deployment can add a requirement later.

values.definition: Open licence that allows the intended use.
Copyright limits copying or adaptation.
A contract or terms of use limit use.
Terms not checked.

basis.note: Creative Commons elements (no derivatives, non-commercial) restrict adaptation and commercial use. The three-value class is inference.

fields.tagging_rule: Write any unless the technique copies, adapts or republishes the material, in which case require open.

fields.label: Primary phase
fields.definition: The one phase in which the technique is normally used. Phases are ordered; the seven-phase list replaces the five steps in the earlier draft.

values.definition: Settle the question, scope, terms and assumptions before evidence is examined.
Find, collect and inventory the material.

Check quality and fitness of the material, then clean, extract and structure it. Ends when the material is ready for analysis. Material that cannot be read is reported in the answer basis and the techniques that need it are dropped.
Explore, measure, model, compare or trace relationships in the prepared material.
Check the result before concluding: held-out validation, agreement with a standard, sensitivity and alternative techniques.
State what the findings support, with a confidence label and a one-line reason for each conclusion.
Communicate the conclusion, its limits and the assumptions behind it.

sources.name: Microsoft TDSP lifecycle detail (GitHub copy, secondary)

basis.note: Seven phases are better supported than five because the process models separate verification from gathering and validation from concluding. Phase is a coarse label; the artefact fields enforce order.

fields.tagging_rule: Pick the phase in which the technique produces its main artefact. If a technique is used equally in two phases, pick the earlier one and list the other in other_phases.

fields.label: Other permitted phases
fields.definition: Further phases in which the technique may be used. Excludes the primary phase.

values.definition: Settle the question, scope, terms and assumptions before evidence is examined.
Find, collect and inventory the material.

Check quality and fitness of the material, then clean, extract and structure it. Ends when the material is ready for analysis. Material that cannot be read is reported in the answer basis and the techniques that need it are dropped.
Explore, measure, model, compare or trace relationships in the prepared material.
Check the result before concluding: held-out validation, agreement with a standard, sensitivity and alternative techniques.
State what the findings support, with a confidence label and a one-line reason for each conclusion.
Communicate the conclusion, its limits and the assumptions behind it.
No other phase.

basis.note: The CIA Primer and KDD show that some techniques are used at the start and revisited later, so one phase is not enough.

fields.tagging_rule: List every other phase in which the technique is a normal choice. Write none if it is used in the primary phase only.

fields.label: Insight type
fields.definition: What the output is read for. Several values are allowed; matching uses it as a weight because tags are inferred.

values.definition: A regularity in the material.
How cases, periods or sources differ.
Statements or sources that cannot both be true.
A cause or effect relationship.
Direction of change over time.
Something expected that is missing.
What could go wrong or where a source is weak.
Options placed in order.

basis.note: Carried over from the earlier reports; all values are the note authors' inference.

fields.tagging_rule: List every insight type the output is read for, with the main one first. Write any only if the technique is general purpose.

fields.label: Question answered
fields.definition: The question the output addresses. Several values are allowed.

values.definition: What is the case, or what is in the material.
Why something happened.
The size of a quantity or effect.
What is likely to happen.
Which actors matter.
Which choice is best.

basis.note: Carried over from the earlier reports; all values are the note authors' inference.

fields.tagging_rule: List every question the output answers, with the main one first.

fields.label: Claim ceiling
fields.definition: The strongest claim the technique can support under ideal conditions. It is a maximum for the technique. The answer does not lower it or judge the material. In the matching step this field never removes a technique. The skill reports how many techniques that passed the other gates reach the claim level needed, and warns when none does, because preparation and appraisal techniques support a stronger final claim without reaching it themselves. The claim level needed also adds checks by stakes tier.

values.definition: Summarise what is in the material or the world without relating variables.
Show that variables, events or claims go together, without saying why.
Forecast or classify new cases from patterns. The prediction never supports a causal reading.
Estimate how an outcome changes when an intervention is applied (Pearl rung 2, Maryland levels 3 to 5, Nesta level 3).
Say how or why, or what would have happened otherwise in a case (Pearl rung 3, Nesta level 4).

basis.note: Changed from hard gate to advisory in consolidation. As a hard gate it removed structuring and appraisal techniques and cut recall (8 of 32 expected picks passed the filter in the first run; 30 of 32 after the change).

fields.tagging_rule: Pick the highest claim level the technique can support if every assumption is met. A technique that only summarises is describe, even if users misuse it for cause.

fields.label: Requires minimum amounts
fields.definition: Minimum amounts the technique needs, such as sample size, number of variables, number of sources or number of periods. Free text so that each can carry its own unit.

basis.note: No source specifies minimums for the catalogue. Stationarity and minimum sample size preconditions were not researched.

fields.tagging_rule: Write each minimum with its unit, for example at least 30 records per group. Write none if no minimum is known.

fields.label: Material needed from outside the input
fields.definition: What the user must supply that the input does not contain. None cannot be combined with other values.

values.definition: Nothing beyond the input.
A second case, group, period or standard to compare with.
A codebook, schema, rule set, protocol or population benchmark.
Data or documents from before the period of interest.

basis.note: Carried over from the earlier reports.

fields.tagging_rule: List what must be supplied. Write none if the input is enough.

fields.label: Not for rules
fields.definition: Machine-checkable exclusions. The technique is removed when all clauses of any one exclusion are true for the job.

sources.name: Liu et al., lost in the middle, arXiv 2307.03172

basis.note: Encoding exclusions as rules is based on the finding that models handle negated conditions poorly; the benefit is untested.

fields.tagging_rule: Write each exclusion as clauses of the form facet=value or facet=value1|value2 joined by &, exclusions separated by ;, and a reason after ::. Keys may be any facet key or claim_level_needed, stakes_tier, insight_wanted. Write none if there are no exclusions.

fields.label: Not for, in words
fields.definition: Fit test and misuse signs that cannot be written as rules, in words. Carried over from the fit test column of the earlier reports.

basis.note: Fit tests in the earlier reports are the note authors' inference except where a row cited a source.

fields.tagging_rule: Write signs that the technique is the wrong choice or is being misused, in one or two sentences. Do not repeat anything already in not_for_rules.

fields.label: Consumes
fields.definition: Artefacts the technique reads, each with the state it needs, written as type:state. An artefact type marked single use is spent by the first technique that consumes it.

basis.note: Order follows from artefact preconditions as in CWL data links and PROV used. Single use follows Egami et al.: the test set is used once. Typed artefact list is partly design choice.

fields.tagging_rule: List each artefact the technique needs before it can start, as type:state. If the technique starts from the user's question alone, write charter or question:agreed.

fields.label: Produces
fields.definition: Artefacts the technique creates, each with the state it reaches, written as type:state.

sources.name: Microsoft TDSP lifecycle detail (GitHub copy, secondary)

basis.note: Mirrors TDSP stage artefacts and PROV generated entities.

fields.tagging_rule: List each artefact the technique outputs, as type:state. Every technique produces at least one artefact.

fields.label: Requires
fields.definition: Hard prerequisites beyond the artefacts consumed: technique IDs that must have run, or artefact types that must exist, written as artefact:type:state. The technique must not run until all are met.

basis.note: After CWL requirements, which must be met before a process runs, as distinct from hints.

fields.tagging_rule: Write technique IDs or artefact:type:state items separated by ;. Do not repeat artefacts already in consumes. Write none if there is no extra prerequisite.

fields.label: Related techniques
fields.definition: Soft and conditional relations to other techniques, one item per relation, written as relation :: ID :: reason. Relations are should follow, substitutes for, pairs with and conflicts with, defined in the relations section.

values.definition: Better run after the named technique or family, for the reason given.
Gives the same artefact with different assumptions, under the condition named.
Covers a named weakness of the other technique when run alongside it.
Cannot both be applied to the same artefact instance, or one consumes what the other needs.

basis.note: No standard defines these relations for analytical techniques. The only evidence is prose in the CIA Primer and the Futures Toolkit, and the test-set rule in Egami et al.

fields.tagging_rule: Write each item as relation :: ID or family name :: one-line reason, items separated by ;. Substitutes for must name the facet condition in the reason. Write none if there are no relations.

fields.label: Loop target
fields.definition: What happens when the technique's fit test fails. Exactly one outcome.

values.definition: Continue and record the failed fit test as a limit on the claim.
Rework the question or scope.
Collect more or different material.
Clean, extract or restructure the material again.
Try another technique or settings on the same prepared material.

values.value: stop because the data cannot answer the question
values.definition: Report the limit; do not continue.

sources.name: Microsoft TDSP lifecycle detail (GitHub copy, secondary)

basis.note: Three-way outcome after TDSP checkpoints; named return targets follow TDSP, whereas KDD allows loops between any steps.

fields.tagging_rule: Pick the outcome that follows a failed fit test. Use stop only when no earlier phase can repair the failure.

fields.label: Model suitability
fields.definition: The most demanding level of support the whole technique needs, from least to most oversight. The skill compares it with what the deployment offers.

values.definition: A language model can do every step with no code and no person.
Needs code execution for at least one step, such as arithmetic or sampling.
Needs a person to supply or confirm a judgement.

basis.note: Carried over from the earlier reports; all values are the note authors' inference.

fields.tagging_rule: Pick the most demanding level any step needs. If one step needs a human judgement, write human judgement required.

fields.label: Typical model failure
fields.definition: The most likely way an AI model gets this technique wrong, in words.

basis.note: Grimmer and Stewart: all quantitative models of language are wrong, so validation is required. Failure descriptions are the tagger's inference.

fields.tagging_rule: Write one or two sentences naming a specific failure, for example inventing a source or miscounting. Write unknown if no failure is known.

fields.label: Repeatability
fields.definition: How far the same input gives the same output.

values.definition: The same input always gives the same output.
The same input gives the same output when settings such as seed or temperature are fixed.
Output depends on a person's or a model's judgement and varies between runs or between people.

basis.note: No published framework uses this classification.

definitions.definition: The output decides what to look at next. A wrong result costs little and is corrected before anyone relies on it.

tiers.tier_rule: Each technique lists its own minimum checks per tier in minimum_checks. Each higher tier contains every check of the tier below. Pick the tier from what the decision costs if wrong and whether it can be reversed, using criteria the user can answer.

tiers.stop_rule: If a library check required at the high-stakes level fails, the confidence label for each conclusion that depends on it is low and the reason names the check. A check that needs a person and was not done is listed in the answer as not done. At the high-stakes level it limits the label to medium until a person does it. At lower levels it is named in the reason and does not change the label.

corroboration_rule.definition: Every technique in a run reads the same material and is run by the same model, so two techniques cannot be independent in data or model. Two techniques count as having different methods when they read the material in different ways, for example one counts cases and one searches for disconfirming statements. The model states the difference in the reason for the confidence label. Agreement between techniques with different methods supports a high label. Agreement between techniques that do not have different methods is reported as consistency and supports a medium label at most. Repeat runs and prompt variation test stability and are reported as consistency. The answer states the shared material and model as a limit.
corroboration_rule.machine_test: Two techniques do not have different methods when either is tagged as substitutes for the other in related_techniques, or when they are the same technique run twice. Otherwise the model decides and states the difference in one line.
corroboration_rule.hypothesis_not_tested: Outputs from one language model reviewing another may share training-related biases. No source was found; this is a hypothesis.

steps: Step 1, intake: turn the user input into a brief (request, settings, material and description of the material). Unknown properties that a requirement tests become questions before step 2.

Step 2: apply the personal information requirement against the description of the material. A technique that cannot take personal information is kept, with a note, when de-identification is in the plan and runs before it. It is removed when the material is marked sensitive and the user has not agreed to de-identify. Security classification and licence are not used: every technique is tagged any.

Apply hard gates on content type, unit of analysis, access depth, number of sources and linkage. Units of analysis that a preparation step can derive (document to claim or source, record to variable or dataset, dataset to variable, source to document) pass with a note. A technique that fails only on content type or representation passes when every prepared artefact it consumes is produced by a technique that passed the gates. It carries a note naming the technique that must run first. Access depth, units and the other gates are not waived.

Apply conditional gates when their conditions are met: representation, time structure, collection basis, volume class, data condition flags, language, requires_minimum and material needed from outside the input.

Apply not_for_rules and requires. A technique whose consumed artefact cannot exist yet, or that needs external material (comparator, reference structure, earlier period), is kept with a note naming what is missing. The external material is gathered in stage 1 only for techniques that were picked.
Claim ceiling raises a warning only: count the eligible techniques that reach the strength of statement needed and warn when none does.

Step 3: give the model the brief and a one-line entry (ID, name, purpose, use when) for every eligible technique, ordered by a score for insight type, prefers items and evidence status. The score does not cut the list, because a score-ranked shortlist of 15 found 8 of 32 expected picks and the model reading the full list found 22 of 32. The model chooses at most 10 (sequencing limits), using four criteria in order: (1) every part of the request has at least one technique; (2) at least one technique reaches the strength of statement needed when an eligible one fits the request, and if none fits the model says so with the reason; (3) the techniques match the kind of finding wanted, where given; (4) where two techniques serve the same part of the request, prefer a pair with different methods. Each choice has a one-line reason naming the part of the request it serves.
Step 4: place the chosen techniques in one sequence by kind, with a description of what each group does (sequencing section) and attach library checks from the stakes and strength of statement rules.
matching.multiple_sources: When source-level facets differ between sources, a requires is met only if every source meets it. A prefers is scored by the share of sources that meet it.

packaging.status: All recommendations below are inference and untested. No source tested a 234 technique catalogue, a CSV queried by script, or contraindication fields.

basis.note: Sourced facts are listed under documented_limits; the design built on them is inference.

documented_limits: SKILL.md body should be under 500 lines (Anthropic skills guidance).
Reference files should be one level deep from SKILL.md, and files over 100 lines should start with a table of contents.
The description must be non-empty, at most 1,024 characters, and state what the skill does and when to use it.
Custom frontmatter such as metadata is not acted on by Claude Code, so per-technique fields cannot affect whether the skill triggers.
The Claude API runtime has no network access and no package installation, so a filtering script must use only installed packages.
recommendations: SKILL.md contains the procedure and a compact index of one line per technique (ID, name, family, purpose, use when). It does not contain the full records.
Full records (what it does, fit test, output specification, checks, failure modes) are in reference files, one per family, one level deep, each with a table of contents.
A CSV with one column per field key is queried by scripts: intake.py (profile and gap questions), select.py (gates), sequence.py (stages, checks, synthesis block). Only script output enters context.
Contraindications are stored as not_for_rules so code applies them. Only 14 of 236 rows use them so far.
Add a full method card to a technique only where a test run shows the output specification is not enough. The first test found it unnecessary for five techniques.
Build a larger test set of briefs with known correct techniques, and measure the index-reading recall and final choice accuracy against a baseline without the skill, with more than one model size.
packaging.draft_skill_description: Selects analytical techniques for a research question and the material available, puts them in a workable order, and states the checks each result needs. Use when a user asks which analysis or approach to apply to documents, reports, survey data, tables, interviews or web sources, how to sequence several analyses, how reliable a finding is, or how much checking an AI-assisted analysis needs. Covers 234 techniques for framing, comparison, causal and claim testing, evidence handling, forecasting, risk assessment, text and data preparation, modelling, source integration and result checking.

sequencing.rule: Every technique belongs to one of five kinds, and the kind decides what it works on. A question technique works on the request (5.1). A preparation technique works on the material and produces prepared material (5.2). A primary technique works on the material, including prepared material, and never on another primary technique's result (5.3). Verification and challenge techniques work on the findings of the analysis (step 6). Combining the findings (step 7) is a fixed process step, not a technique. Only the user changes the request.
stages: 5.1 examine the question: chosen techniques whose phase is frame. When they produce findings, the process shows them and asks the user to keep or edit the request. Keep: the run continues at 5.2. Edit: steps 2 to 4 run again on the new request, and question techniques that already ran are not chosen again. No reply: the request stays as it is and the answer says it was not confirmed. The findings are kept in every case and go to step 7.

5.2 prepare the material: chosen techniques whose phase is gather or verify and prepare, any technique that produces prepared material a chosen technique consumes, and de-identification when the material has personal information. Prepared material is still the brief's material. For each chosen technique that needs outside material (a comparator, a reference structure or an earlier period), 5.2 looks in the user's content first. If the item is not there, it finds the one item needed, from a source that is not marketing or personal opinion, or asks the user for it. The user approves the item before any technique uses it. If none is found or approved, the technique is dropped and the answer says so.
5.3 analyse the material: chosen primary techniques, independent of each other, run in any order, each on the brief.

6 check the findings: chosen verification techniques, then chosen challenge techniques, each on the findings of the analysis, then the library checks for the stakes and the strength of statement, each applied to one result.

7 combine the findings (process step): collect the findings; run a method from the synthesis section (the process offers those that apply and recommends one); name the cause of each conflict or state that it is unresolved; give each conclusion a confidence label and a one-line reason.

8 answer: give the conclusions, the strength of statement reached, and what the answer is based on. Offer a follow-up round. If the user accepts, steps 2 to 4 run again for the gaps and unresolved conflicts found in step 7, leaving out techniques that already ran and starting from the reserve list, then the new techniques run and steps 6 to 8 are repeated with all the findings. The process never starts a follow-up round on its own.

basis.note: Designed with the user in this session; untested on real jobs.

limits.definition: The model chooses at most 10 techniques in the first round, listed in priority order. All kinds of technique count. Preparation techniques added for a chosen technique, de-identification and library checks do not count. Techniques the model wanted beyond the limit go on the reserve list and are offered in a follow-up round. Each follow-up round adds at most 5.

basis.note: Limit set with the user on 11 November 2026. The numbers are defaults chosen by the schema designer, not measured.

plan_reasons.definition: The plan is one sequence in four groups. Each technique's kind decides its group and position. The plan records a name for each group, a note where the order matters to the user, the reason for each chosen technique (from step 3) and the reason for each addition (a preparation technique, de-identification or outside material). The records are kept so that the answer can describe the process followed. The groups do no work themselves. The techniques do, so the plan describes what each technique does, not what a group does.

positions.note: If a technique finds a problem with the question, you see it and can change the question before the rest runs.

positions.kind: verification and challenge techniques, then library checks

plan_table.definition: Step 4 shows the plan as a table of techniques under four group headings, in running order and without numbers. The group headings are Clarify the question, Prepare the content, Analyse the content and Test the findings. Columns: the technique, what the technique does (the catalogue's one-sentence purpose) and whether it needs outside material (none, comparator, reference structure or earlier period). A group heading carries a note only where the order matters to the user. Step 4 only records the need for outside material. It does not gather anything.

basis.note: Decided with the user on 13 November 2026.

synthesis.definition: Synthesis is the final process step. It takes the findings of the independent analyses as its input, not the brief's material. No single agreed framework exists for synthesising diverse findings, and the choice of method depends on the aim and the form of the findings, so the skill offers the methods that apply and recommends one.

sources.name: Dixon-Woods et al. 2005, Synthesising qualitative and quantitative evidence: a review of possible methods (PubMed abstract)
Mays, Pope and Popay 2005, methodological appendix on approaches to synthesis (LSHTM repository abstract)

basis.note: The sources review methods for synthesising evidence from studies. Applying them to the findings of techniques within one job is an extrapolation by the schema designer. Abstracts and summary pages only were read.

findings_form.definition: Derived from the material content types: textual (text only), numeric (tabular, time series or similar only), mixed (both).

commensurable_estimates.definition: Asked of the user. Yes only if two or more findings are estimates of the same quantity on the same scale.

methods.name: convergence matrix
methods.what_it_does: Lists each technique's findings side by side by theme or question, and marks each as agreement, partial agreement, dissonance or silence. Disagreement is kept as information. Two analysts compare the matrix and resolve differences by discussion.
methods.applies_when: Two or more analytical techniques were run. Any findings_form.
methods.output: A matrix of findings against techniques, with a global assessment of convergence and a list of dissonant findings.
methods.limits: It marks agreement but does not weigh findings. Counting how many techniques mention a theme is not a measure of strength.

sources.name: O'Cathain, Murphy and Nicholl 2010, Three techniques for integrating data in mixed methods studies, BMJ
Tonkin-Crine et al. 2016, triangulation protocol applied to a trial process evaluation, Implementation Science (PMC)

basis.note: Triangulation protocol and convergence coding matrix, from mixed methods health research. Applying it across techniques is an extrapolation.

methods.name: narrative synthesis
methods.what_it_does: Summarises, compares, explains and interprets the findings in words, keeping each finding in its own terms. Used to write the answer to the question once the matrix shows where findings agree and conflict.
methods.recommended_when: findings_form is textual or mixed, after the convergence matrix
methods.output: A written answer that states each conclusion, the findings behind it and the conflicts left unresolved.
methods.limits: Without a stated structure it can hide which findings were given more weight. State the weighting rule used.

sources.name: Mays, Pope and Popay 2005, methodological appendix on approaches to synthesis (LSHTM repository abstract)

basis.note: Narrative synthesis described as one of four basic approaches.

methods.name: quantitative pooling
methods.what_it_does: Combines findings that are estimates of the same quantity into one estimate, by meta-analysis or Bayesian updating, with an interval.
methods.recommended_when: findings_form is numeric and commensurable_estimates is yes
methods.output: A pooled estimate with an interval, and a measure of how much the findings differ.
methods.limits: Findings that share a scale but not a design or a population should not be pooled. The pooled interval is too narrow when the estimates are not independent.

sources.name: Dixon-Woods et al. 2005, Synthesising qualitative and quantitative evidence: a review of possible methods (PubMed abstract)

basis.note: Quantitative and Bayesian approaches named among the available methods.

methods.name: decision analysis and weighting
methods.what_it_does: Turns findings and stated preferences into weights and scores for the options, and ranks the options.
methods.output: A ranking of the options with the weights and scores shown.
methods.limits: The weights come from the decision maker, not the evidence. Show how the ranking changes when the weights change.

sources.name: Mays, Pope and Popay 2005, methodological appendix on approaches to synthesis (LSHTM repository abstract)

basis.note: Decision analysis named among the four basic approaches.

certainty_rating.definition: Not a synthesis method. Each conclusion in the answer gets one confidence label (high, medium or low) and a one-line reason. The user reads the label to decide whether to trust the conclusion or redo the work. No likelihood terms and no roll-up across conclusions.
certainty_rating.rule: High: two or more techniques with different methods (tiers.corroboration_rule) agree, and their checks passed. Medium: one technique supports the conclusion and its checks passed; or two or more techniques agree and a check failed or was not done, or a verification finding limits the conclusion, or the techniques do not have different methods. Low: one technique supports the conclusion and none of its checks passed; or techniques conflict and the conflict is unresolved. A check that failed or was not done is named in the reason. A check not done because it needs a person limits the label to medium at the high-stakes level only. At the high-stakes level a failed check makes the label low (tiers.stop_rule). A challenge finding does not change the label. It is an added finding and appears in the answer next to the conclusion it examines.

basis.note: Simplified with the user on 11 November 2026 and completed on 12 November 2026 (conflicts, checks not done, different methods). The earlier design used GRADE-style certainty and ICD 203 likelihood terms. The rule is a design choice and is untested.

synthesis.offer_to_user: The process lists the methods whose applies_when is met, marks the recommended one with its reason, and asks the user to choose or accept the recommendation. It runs the recommended method if the user does not reply.

answer_basis.definition: The answer states three things as facts and makes no judgement about the material. (1) Strength of statement reached: which chosen techniques reach the strength of statement the user needed and which conclusions they support; when none did, the answer says so in its first lines. (2) What the answer is based on: what the user gave (each source, its type and size), any outside material gathered and where from, which techniques ran and what each worked on (the request, the material, or the findings of the analysis), which techniques were dropped and why, any files that could not be read, any checks that were not done, taken from the check library field human_involvement (needed, or conditional when the condition applies), and whether the user confirmed the request after 5.1. (3) The offer of a follow-up round. It does not say whether the material is representative or sufficient.

basis.note: Decided with the user on 11 November 2026. Replaces the earlier idea of a material ceiling on the claim level.

interaction.definition: Where the skill asks the user and where it decides.

asks.what: The request restated in one sentence, the strength of statement needed and the stakes. The process asks only for properties the material does not show.

Asked only when question techniques ran and produced findings. The process shows the findings and asks the user to keep or edit the request. An edit runs steps 2 to 4 again. With no reply the request stays as it is and the answer says it was not confirmed.

Asked only when a chosen technique needs outside material that is not in the user's content. The process shows the item and its source. The user approves it before any technique uses it. If none is found or approved, the technique is dropped and the answer says so.
The skill lists the methods whose applies_when is met, marks the recommended one with its reason, and runs it if the user does not reply.
Asked only when two or more numeric findings could estimate the same quantity. Pooling is left out of the list otherwise.
With the answer the process offers a follow-up round for the gaps and unresolved conflicts. It never starts one without the user asking.

decides.what: The model chooses the techniques by the four criteria in matching, code places them in one sequence of four groups with a description of what each group does, and the process shows each choice with a one-line reason. The user can change the list but is not asked to choose from it.

basis.note: Agreed with the user in this session. Untested with real users.

output_and_work.definition: The answer given in step 8 is the only output and is always given to the user. It must be complete without the work, so it names the techniques that ran and the checks that were not done. Everything produced in steps 1 to 7 is work: the description of the material, the eligible and chosen techniques, the sequence, each technique's result, the checks and the combined findings. The work is kept, and the application that runs the process decides how much of it the user sees (as it happens, on request, or not at all). Where the process asks the user to decide something, it always shows what the user needs for that decision. The user can change the chosen techniques only in an application that shows them.

basis.note: Decided with the user on 13 November 2026.

intake.definition: Step 1. Turns the user input into a brief and lists the gaps as questions. The brief is the request, the settings (stakes, strength of statement needed, kind of finding wanted), the material and the description of the material. The request can have several parts or be open-ended (for example "tell me what insights I can get from this article"), and step 3 returns one set of techniques for it. Each chosen technique states which part of the request it serves. For an open-ended request the kind of finding is left empty and the strength of statement defaults to describe.

inputs.input: link to an article or report
inputs.acquired_by: The model reads the page with the page fetch tool and saves the text with a sidecar file (URL, title, publisher, date, fetched_by). The fetch tool can summarise long pages, so intake flags that quotes are unverified against the page and asks for the document as a file when the stakes are above exploratory.

inputs.input: content pasted from an article or report
inputs.acquired_by: Saved as text with origin_type pasted.
Under 40 words it is the question. Longer typed text is material.
Files or a folder: txt, md, html, docx, pdf, csv, tsv, xlsx. Unreadable files are listed.

inferred_with_note: privacy as none for report-type documents with no personal signals
claim_level_needed and insight_wanted from question wording
intake.question_rules: At most four questions at once, in priority order, each with a recommended answer where one exists and a one-line reason. The rest are held back.

basis.note: Designed with the user on 11 November 2026. Run on four small test inputs; one used made-up transcripts.

application.definition: Each selected technique runs on the brief, independently of the others. The model is given the technique record and its output specification and writes a result in that shape.
application.rule: A full method card is not written for any technique unless a test run shows the record and output specification produce a wrong or incomplete result.
application.test: Five techniques were each run with the row only and with the row plus an output specification, and scored blind against eight-item checklists written by the schema designer: 33 of 40 without and 37 of 40 with. One run per cell, so the gap is within noise. The specification helped most for absence analysis and disconfirmation search.

basis.note: Test of 11 November 2026. The specifications and checklists were written by the same author, so the result may favour the specification.

check_library_note: human_involvement says whether a check needs a person. needed: the process cannot do it and lists it in the answer basis as not done. optional: code or the model can do it, and a person can too. conditional: needed only when the stated condition holds. none: the process does it.

steps.name: Intake
steps.does: The user's input becomes a brief. Gaps become questions to the user.

steps.name: Rule out techniques
steps.does: Each technique is tested against the brief. Techniques that cannot run on the material are removed. The rest are eligible.

steps.name: Choose analysis techniques
steps.does: The model reads a list of the eligible techniques and chooses at most 10, with a reason for each.

steps.name: Plan analysis sequence
steps.does: The chosen techniques are placed in four named groups in running order, each technique with a description of what it does and a note of whether it needs outside material. Preparation techniques and checks are added.

steps.name: Run the techniques
steps.does: 5.1 Examine the question. 5.2 Prepare the material, including any outside material, which the user approves. 5.3 Analyse the material.

steps.name: Check the findings
steps.does: Verification and challenge techniques run on the findings. The library checks are applied to each result.

steps.name: Combine the findings
steps.does: The findings become conclusions. Each conclusion gets a confidence label and a one-line reason.

steps.name: Answer
steps.does: The answer is given with a list of what it is based on. The user can ask for a follow-up round.

terms.note: The schema and scripts keep their original field names and values. This list gives the name used in the design document and on the site for each.
map: strength of statement needed, strongest statement a technique supports
estimate the effect of an action
working document; needs as input; makes as output
what the answer is based on
